"The Graduate Admissions Committee in the Department of English at the University of Florida has completed its review of applications and, unfortunately, has not selected you for admission.
 
This is no reflection on your academic excellence. We received more than 200 applications from talented and accomplished students all over the world for our graduate program, and we have admitted fewer than 10%. With so many excellent applicants to choose from, our decisions often came down to judgments about which students we can best support with our particular faculty expertise, our library resources, and the teaching and other training opportunities we can provide. Many of those who applied to our program can, we believe, actually be served better elsewhere. We hope that you get that opportunity, and we wish you luck and success in your future endeavors.
 
One final note: because we had so many applicants, we are unable to offer each applicant a detailed response on our Admissions Committee’s decision. Dear Applicant,
Thank you for the time, effort, and passion you put into your application to the UCSC Physics graduate program. There is a person behind every application, statement of purpose, and letter of recommendation, and we truly appreciate the effort you contributed applying to our program. That is what makes it challenging to inform you we are unable to recommend you for admission for this coming fall.

This was a difficult decision for our committee for two reasons: 1) this year’s applicant pool was exceptionally talented, and the level of research experience and academic dedication we saw was genuinely humbling; and 2) due to department funding and faculty research capacity we are simply unable to recommend offers of admission to all researchers we believe would thrive here.

This decision is a reflection of our departmental constraints, not a reflection of your potential as a physicist. There are many paths towards scientific inquiry, and we hope you continue pursuing your interests in physics research.

Understandably, many applicants ask us for feedback on their applications to see how they can improve in the future. Please understand due to the sheer number of requests we receive the committee is unable to provide comment on any individual's application. We trust that your continued efforts and dedication will open doors for you as you pursue your career.

Thank you again for considering UC Santa Cruz. We wish you the very best in your next chapter.
MSR

This rejection was always coming. Anyway, I have accepted another top-tier offer from elsewhere, so it doesn't matter anymore. But to anyone reading this: please do not, DO NOT apply to NUS ECE without explicit PI interest, especially if you're thinking of doing so straight out of undergrad.

comments: I had a very disappointing experience applying to the PhD program in EECS at the University of Wyoming. I submitted my application in January and never received any clear communication regarding its completeness. There were no notifications about missing documents, and every time I reached out for a status update, I received vague or delayed responses. In several instances, there was no reply at all. The lack of professionalism from the department, including the Graduate Coordinator, was frustrating. As an applicant investing significant time, effort, and money into the process, I expected at least basic transparency and communication. Unfortunately, that standard was not met. What makes this worse is that the final rejection cited multiple concerns, but none of these were ever communicated earlier in the process, nor was there any opportunity to clarify or strengthen the application. It raises serious questions about how thoroughly applications are handled and whether they are reviewed in a timely and organized manner. Overall, the experience felt disorganized, dismissive, and disrespectful toward applicants. Based on this experience, I would strongly caution prospective students to think carefully before applying here. Applicants deserve timely communication, clear guidance, and professional treatment—none of which I experienced in this process.

I emailed asking when I might get my decision because it seems late.  They emailed back very promptly saying it should be in the portal.  I responded that when I log in to ApplyWeb, on the page where I can see all the universities that used ApplyWeb, there is a "decision letter" button above the "checklist" button but this doesn't appear for Cornell.  They responded that perhaps it needs to process overnight, but let them know if I still didn't see it tomorrow.  I talked to the tech support bot which suggests (Interesting to know!) that universities load a bunch of decision letters and then have to add a date and time and give permission for the student to view it (so if the college says it's there and I say it's not, they probably didn't give permission yet).  I sent that info to the kind administrative person at Cornell's History Graduate program, who thanked me for it and said it gave them an idea of a few things to go check.  Sounds like the funding cuts really hit a lot of areas -- my home department has had a lot of cuts and it's our admin person who is bearing the brunt of a lot of it.  Anyway.  Still can't see a decision in the portal, but it's apparent my application is just an administrative loose end, and this cycle has taught me that my research niche is "weird" and difficult for programs to find space for.  1a/7r/3p is I think the current tally, one pending is a Public Policy program.

"Thank you for applying to the Ph.D. program in Quantum Science and Engineering at the University of Chicago for the 2026 academic year. While we are unable to offer you admission, we recognize and commend your academic and personal achievements. This year’s applicant pool was one of our largest and most competitive with many highly qualified applicants for a limited number of spaces. Nonetheless, our faculty admissions committee was enthusiastic about your application, and we have asked the Master of Engineering (M.Eng.) program to consider your application for admission.

Ph.D. applicants of great promise, such as yourself, are referred by the faculty to the Master of Engineering program, where students can make the most of rigorous coursework among our Ph.D. students and the talented students in the M.Eng. program. Graduates go on to pursue doctoral work at highly ranked programs (including our own), while others discover a career aspiration that they hadn’t previously considered.

The admissions committee is currently reviewing applications with an eye to intellectual promise, academic accomplishment, and fit for this intensive master’s program in the Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering. Please consider this letter as a formal acknowledgement that you have been placed on our short and selective
waitlist for the MFA Program in Creative Writing at The Ohio State University. All of us on the faculty here
greatly admire your work and would be delighted to have you with us next year should a spot open. 

The truth is, determining “who gets in” versus “who gets waitlisted” once we have agreed on a group of writers
we want to admit is always ridiculously difficult. This is an inexact business (and of course it’s not a “business”
at all), and ours is a very small program by design. Please be aware that you are among a distinguished group of
writers who received enthusiastic “yes” votes from every one of the relevant faculty. 

I can promise you that the very latest you will hear from us about your admission will be one week after April
15, which is the date by which all admitted students must either decline or accept our offer. It’s very possible
that you will hear from us sooner, but I wouldn’t count on that, as many people wait until the last possible
minute to say yes or no. All I can tell you for sure is that as soon as we know how many offers have been
accepted, I will contact you one way or the other.

Status: Conditionally Accepted (Full-Time)

Notes:
Received a conditional offer for the MSc in Environmental Economics and Climate Change at LSE for the 2025/26 academic year. Program duration is 12 months, from 22 September 2025 to 27 September 2026, with graduation scheduled in December 2026.

Conditions to be met before enrolment:

Submission of final transcript and official documentation confirming completion of Bachelor of Science in Foreign Service (BSFS) from Georgetown University, School of Foreign Service in Qatar.

Minimum GPA requirement: 3.3 out of 4.

Fulfill English language requirement (IELTS overall score of 7.0, with at least 6.5 in each component or equivalent).

Financial details:

Classified as Overseas for tuition purposes; total fees are £35,500 for the 2025/26 session.

Not awarded the Graduate Support Scheme (GSS). Eligible for consideration for other LSE scholarships until July 2025.

Required to complete and submit the Financial Undertaking Form (FUF) by 31 July 2025.

Visa Information:

Need to obtain a Student visa (CAS number issued by LSE from May 2025 onward).

Advised to prepare visa documentation early due to processing times.

Accommodation:

Accommodation available in LSE halls or partner-managed residences with prices ranging approximately from £140 to over £400 per week.

Recommended to budget around £1,400 per month for living expenses, plus £1,000 initial one-off expenses.

Additional Information:

No nomination for ESRC 1+3.5 funding; eligible to apply for MPhil/PhD scholarships after enrolling.

No ATAS clearance required

“I am writing to offer sincere thanks for your application to the Anthropology Ph.D. program at UC Santa Cruz, and to express appreciation for your patience during an unprecedented admissions season.  

This admissions cycle began with our typical (somewhat lengthy) multi-stage review process. As mentioned in my last email, in order to give every application the thorough assessment it deserved, close readings were done by faculty members, which were then discussed with sub-field colleagues, who subsequently shared their impressions with our entire admissions committee.  As Chair of the Anthropology Admissions Committee I always find it exciting to learn about the accomplishments and academic goals of our applicants!

However, very late in the cycle, when departments were preparing to submit acceptance nominations to our Graduate Division, admissions deliberations encountered an atypical wrinkle that further lengthened our deliberations. As you are likely aware, uncertainties around the status of Federal grants and contracts for research and education have impacted the admissions postures of many universities. UC Santa Cruz is among the many institutions adjusting to this budgetary uncertainty, and our Graduate Division determined the need to dramatically scale back admissions for fall 2025. 

This will make for an exceptionally lean admissions picture for UCSC Anthropology – perhaps the most competitive in our program’s history.  While the UCSC Graduate Division will be sending official decision letters very soon, I wanted to communicate with you personally, to thank you for the time and care you gave your application, and to provide context for the difficult decisions we had to make this year.
